newsitem.title: USA: Universal Automotive ups credit to $20mln.
newsitem.headline: Universal Automotive ups credit to $20mln.

text.p: Universal Automotive Industries Inc said Monday ABN AMRO NV's LaSalle National Bank will increased its revolving line of credit to $20 million from $18 million.

The credit facility permits borrowings up to $20 million at the prime rate plus 0.5 percent or the LIBOR rate plus up to 2.5 percent annually, said chief financial officer Jerome Hiss. He expected the deal to close within a week.
Universal said LaSalle will also grant it a $4.5 million term loan, with interest of the prime rate plus 0.75 percent or the LIBOR rate plus 2.75 percent annually.
The maker of brakes and other car parts said the deal is dependent on the company's procuring more than $3 million of subordinate debt financing.
Universal said Sirrom Capital Corp of Nashville, Tenn., financed a $4.5 million five-year subordinated debenture with 12.25 interest annually.

Under the deal, Sirrom will receive a warrant to buy 450,000 Universal shares at an exercise price of 80 percent of the stock's average bid price for 20 days before the first anniversary of the debenture's closing date. Hiss said he expected to close the deal within a week.
Sirrom also will receive warrants to buy 225,000 Universal shares every August until August 2001 under the same conditions, unless the company pays off the debenture, Universal said.
Universal's stock traded at 3 Monday afternoon, up 1/32.
